label.name: Name

notice.failed: The approvals service did not answer. This is not an empty tenant.
notice.detailIsFirstRow: The detail below is the first row of the listing above, read once.
notice.identifiersNotNames: Members, subjects and records are shown by identifier. Resolving one to a person’s name belongs to another module and is not read here.
notice.actionsAreApi: This screen reads only. Raising, deciding, cancelling, publishing and retiring are operations of the approvals API, and the server decides each one.
notice.queueIsAmbient: “Waiting for you” is resolved from the signed-in request. This screen never asks for somebody else’s queue, and there is no field through which it could.
notice.approverIsConfigured: The approver on a step is the member configured to be asked. It is not the person reading this screen.
notice.commentOnDecision: A rejection comment stays on the decision, where a permission decides who may read it. It is never moved into the timeline.
notice.historyIsRouting: The timeline records routing only — who was asked, who answered, and when. A business outcome belongs to the module that owns the record.
notice.subjectIsOpaque: A subject type and a subject identifier are the owning module’s own values. Approvals stores them and interprets neither.
notice.groupIsExplicitList: An approval group is an explicit list of memberships a tenant wrote down. It is not a role, a department, an organizational unit or a directory query, and nothing resolves it from anywhere else.
notice.groupListingIsNotCounted: The listing shows the groups themselves. A member count is a property of one group and is read from its detail below, for the first row only — a count per row would be one request per group.
notice.groupIsSnapshotted: An approval already running keeps the members it started with. Changing a group today does not reach an approval raised yesterday.
notice.tallyIsServerComputed: Every number in a tally is the server’s own count over the decisions that exist. Nothing on this screen adds, divides or compares them, and no percentage is derived from them.
notice.branchIsSimultaneous: Several approvers may share one position and are asked at the same time. A position with more than one approver is one branch, not several steps in order.
notice.conditionIsConfiguration: A condition is shown as it was configured. It is evaluated by the server when an approval starts, never in this screen, and a value the request does not carry is a refusal there rather than a false here.
notice.managerIsConfiguredNotNamed: A manager step names nobody. It means the manager of whoever raises the approval, which is fixed rather than configured, so there is no person, employment or reporting line to show here.
notice.managerIsSnapshotted: The manager is worked out once, when an approval starts, and the person found then stays on that approval for its whole life. A reporting line changed afterwards does not move an approval already running; the next one raised will find the new manager.
notice.serviceLevelIsObserved: A target is a target and not a deadline. Nothing happens when it passes: no approval expires, nobody is reminded and nothing is reassigned. Whether a step is past its target is worked out by the server each time this page is read.
notice.serviceLevelIsElapsedTime: A target counts elapsed time from the moment that step was asked. Two days means forty-eight hours, including weekends and holidays: this product holds no calendar and no working-time rule.

rejection.branch-rule-inconsistent: Every approver asked at the same point must be under the same rule.
rejection.cancellation-reason-required: Stopping an approval needs a reason.

rejection.decision-step-ambiguous: You have been asked more than once here. Choose which step you are answering.

rejection.version-transition-refused: A workflow version cannot move from its current state to that one.

withheld.businessDays: Nothing is calculated in business days. Approvals holds no calendar and no working-time rule.
withheld.escalation: Nothing escalates. A step past its target is shown as past it and nothing follows: no reassignment after a delay, and no next approver on a timer.
withheld.scheduling: Nothing is scheduled. No approval is advanced, closed or reviewed by a background job.
withheld.approvalExpiry: No approval expires. A step may be past its target and stays exactly where it is; `expired` is declared in the approval vocabulary and this phase never produces it.
withheld.delegationExpiry: A delegation is not expired automatically. Whether one is in force is answered when a decision is made.
withheld.roles: There is no role directory and no role approver. A step names a member, an approval group — an explicit list — or the requester’s manager, and never a role.
withheld.externalApprovers: There is no external approver. Everybody asked is a member of this tenant.
withheld.notificationDelivery: Nothing is delivered. No email, message or push notification is sent when somebody is asked to decide.
withheld.analytics: There are no approval analytics. No success rate, average time, bottleneck or compliance figure is calculated anywhere.
withheld.asynchronousCallbacks: There is no asynchronous callback. A decision reaches the module that raised the approval inside the approver’s own request.
withheld.outbox: There is no outbox and no message broker. Nothing is queued for later delivery.
withheld.groupDirectory: There is no group directory. An approval group is a list a tenant maintains; no department, organizational unit or membership query is resolved into one.
withheld.selfServicePortal: There is no self-service or external portal. Approvals are read and decided by members of this tenant through this product.
withheld.routingIntelligence: There is no routing intelligence beyond the rules above. Nothing chooses an approver by workload, history, seniority or prediction.
withheld.delegationManagement: Delegated access is not managed here. Whether somebody may act for an approver is Identity’s answer, asked at the moment a decision is made.

provided.approvalGroups: Workflow approval groups are supported as explicit membership lists. A step may name a group, and the group is resolved into its individual members when an approval starts.
provided.parallelApproval: Parallel approval is supported. Several approvers may occupy one position and are asked at the same time rather than one after another.
provided.branchRules: Unanimous, majority and first-response are supported as branch rules. Each is counted over the approvers the branch was given when the approval started.
provided.quorum: A quorum is supported as a whole number of responses. It is a count and never a proportion, and it gates an approval and a rejection alike.
provided.conditionalBranching: Conditional branching is supported. A branch may carry conditions on values the request supplied, and the server evaluates them when the approval starts.
provided.tally: A branch tally is published: who was asked, who answered, how many approvals the rule needs, and the outcome. It is computed by the server from the decisions and stored nowhere.
provided.managerRouting: A step may ask the requester’s manager. The person is found once, when the approval starts — through their primary employment and its primary reporting line, one level up — and stays on that approval afterwards.
provided.serviceLevel: A step may carry a target of whole hours or days, counted from the moment that step was asked. It is observed rather than enforced: the server reports whether a step is within or past it, and nothing fires when it passes.
